title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Rubinstein System
line: White develops quietly, and Black takes a full share of the center with pawns.

steps.text: The Nimzo-Indian, and White moves the pawn in front of its king one square. It frees a bishop and guards the center.
Castle. Black keeps the choice of when to take the knight.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares, into the center.
Now push the pawn on c7 two squares. It attacks White's pawn on d4 from the side.
Bring the other knight out. It attacks the pawn on d4 too.

also.d5c4: Taking first is a main line too. This lesson goes on with the knight.

steps.after: White pushes a pawn at the bishop.

steps.text: Take the knight. White's pawns end up two on one file.
Take the pawn on c4. White's bishop takes back, having moved twice.
Bring the queen out. It backs up a pawn push in the center.
Now push the pawn in front of your king two squares.
steps.after: Black has its share of the center, and the bishop on c8 can come out.

summary: Against quiet development, Black castles, puts pawns in the center and opens it once its pieces are out.
